useCase.name: Rate a student against the academic skills a subject teaches, beside the overall percentage
useCase.featureRef: 6.13 Competency / standards-based grading — subject skills only

intent.name: subject.skill.define
intent.summary: Define an academic skill a subject teaches in a class. One step, and it cannot be rated against until a rubric is attached.
routesHere: add algebra as a skill of class 8 maths

routesHere.text: class 8 maths mein algebra ko skill ke tor par shamil karo
routesHere.gloss: add algebra as a skill in class 8 maths

routesHere.text: is mazmoon ki skills define kar do
geometry alag skill hai, daal do
routesHere.gloss: geometry is a separate skill, add it

request.text: bache ko rating do
request.gloss: rate the student

routesElsewhere.note: A skill cannot be rated against until a rubric is attached to it (BR-2, E1).

request.text: class mein bache ka rawaiya bhi likho
request.gloss: record the child's classroom conduct as well

routesElsewhere.note: This covers academic subject skills only. Conduct — participation, effort, attentiveness, punctuality — is assessed by the class teacher across all subjects and is not rated here (BR-7).

request.text: khel aur muqablon ka record rakho
request.gloss: keep a record of sports and competitions

routesElsewhere.note: Co-curricular activity is a record of what happened rather than a rating, and is not held here (BR-8).

steps.note: One step. Skills are defined per class as well as per subject (BR-1) — algebra and geometry within Mathematics are skills of that subject in that class, not of the school.

plan.atomicity: One write: the skill and the audit entry together or not at all. Nothing can be rated against it until a rubric of achievement bands is attached (BR-2, E1) — a rating with no rubric behind it is a number nobody can interpret.

parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters. An academic skill the subject teaches (BR-1). The Coordinator's — what a subject teaches is a curricular judgement, not something to derive from a syllabus heading.

parameters.name: order
parameters.notes: Where it sits among the subject's skills.

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.description: False. It cannot be rated against until a rubric is attached (BR-2, E1).

errors.meaning: The skill describes classroom conduct rather than an academic skill.
errors.note: Accepted, but conduct is assessed by the class teacher across all subjects and is not rated here (BR-7). Report it rather than silently accepting.

errors.meaning: The skill describes a co-curricular activity.
errors.note: Co-curricular activity is a record of what happened, not a rating, and is not held here (BR-8). Report it.

planningRules.rule: Never name the skills a subject teaches. What algebra covers in class 8 is a curricular judgement (BR-1), and a planner that generated a list of skills has written part of the curriculum.

Report where the skill reads as conduct or as a co-curricular activity. Both are accepted (E5, E6), but neither belongs here — conduct is assessed across all subjects by the class teacher, and activity is a record of what happened rather than a rating (BR-7, BR-8).
Say plainly that nothing can be rated yet. A skill with no rubric cannot be rated against (BR-2, E1), and a Coordinator who defines six skills and stops has left teachers with nothing to use.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A skill is retired with a reason rather than deleted, and the ratings already given against it stay readable (BR-9). There is no delete control (E7).

request.text: class 8 maths mein algebra aur geometry ko skills ke tor par shamil karo
request.gloss: add algebra and geometry as skills in class 8 maths

resolvedPlans.context: Coordinator, Johar Town branch. One call per skill.

steps.note: The skill names are the Coordinator's (PR-1). Geometry follows as its own call.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Defined. Report that neither can be rated against until a rubric of bands is attached (PR-3) — a rating with no rubric is a number nobody can interpret.

request.text: is mazmoon ki skills khud bana do
request.gloss: work out this subject's skills yourself

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The skills have nothing to take them from (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is defined. Ask which skills the subject teaches in that class — the answer decides what every teacher rates every student against, and it is a curricular judgement.

request.text: punctuality ko bhi skill mein daal do
request.gloss: add punctuality as a skill as well

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API accepts it and returns CONDUCT_SKILL (E5) on the success path.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Defined, and it works. But report plainly (PR-2) that punctuality is conduct, not an academic skill of maths — it is assessed by the class teacher across all subjects, and rating it here means every subject teacher rates it separately for the same child.

intent.name: subject.skill.rubric.attach
intent.summary: Attach the achievement bands a skill is rated on, each stating what it means. One step.
routesHere: attach the rubric — Beginning, Developing, Secure, Excelling

routesHere.text: is skill ke bands laga do
rubric bana do — har band ka matlab bhi likho
routesHere.gloss: create the rubric — with what each band means

request.text: bache ko band do
request.gloss: rate the student at a band

request.text: purani rating badal do
request.gloss: change the ratings already given

routesElsewhere.note: Changing a band's meaning does not change a rating already given. The rubric in force when the rating was made is recorded with it (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. Every band states what it means, so a parent reading Developing can see what the school means by it (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A band with no description arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the bands and the audit entry together or not at all. Ratings already given keep the rubric that was in force when they were made (BR-10) — rewording a band does not requalify a child who was rated last term.

parameters.name: bands
parameters.notes: Each band: its name, what it means and where it sits from lowest to highest (BR-2, BR-3, E2). Every word is the Coordinator's — a band description a planner wrote is the school telling parents what Developing means.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: A band was saved with no description.
errors.note: A parent reading the band must be able to see what the school means by it (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Never write a band or its description. What Secure means at this school reaches parents as the explanation of their child's rating (BR-3), and a planner's wording is the school saying something nobody decided.
Never reuse a rubric from another skill without being asked. Bands that fit a writing skill may say nothing useful about a numerical one.
Report that ratings already given are unchanged. The rubric in force when a rating was made is recorded with it (BR-10), so rewording a band does not requalify a child rated last term.

resolvedPlans.context: Coordinator, Johar Town branch, on a skill with ratings already given.

intent.name: subject.skill.rate
intent.summary: Rate a student at a band of a skill's rubric, with a note where the band alone does not explain it. One step.
routesHere: rate Ayesha as Secure in algebra

routesHere.text: Ayesha ko algebra mein Secure do
routesHere.gloss: rate Ayesha as Secure in algebra

routesHere.text: is bache ki skill rating laga do

request.text: is skill par rating nahi de sakte
request.gloss: we have no basis for rating this skill

routesElsewhere.note: A rating is optional per student where the teacher has no basis for one, and an unrated skill reads as unrated rather than as the lowest band (BR-11).

request.text: number bhi badal do
request.gloss: change the mark as well

routesElsewhere.note: The ratings sit alongside the subject's marks and are read together, but neither changes the other (BR-5, BR-6).

request.text: rating walidain ko dikha do
request.gloss: show the rating to the parents

routesElsewhere.note: The ratings are released with the result, and not before (BR-12, E8).

steps.note: One step. The subject teacher rates each student against each skill of their own subject (BR-4) — a teacher does not rate a subject they do not teach.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A subject the actor does not teach, and a band that is not on that skill's rubric, arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the rating, its note and the rubric in force together or not at all (BR-10). It is stored alongside that subject's marks so the two are read together (BR-5), and released with the result and not before — a skill profile visible earlier is a result released early by another name (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never infer the band from the mark. The rating says something the percentage does not — that is the whole reason for it (BR-6) — and a band derived from a score is the score again in different words.
Never rate a skill the teacher left alone. An unrated skill reads as unrated rather than as the lowest band (BR-11), and filling it in puts a judgement on a child that nobody made.
Never write the note. It reaches the family with the result, and it is the teacher's account of what the band alone does not explain.
Report the skills still unrated for that student. They read as unrated, which is honest — but a teacher who meant to rate all six should see that three are missing.
Never describe a rating as visible. Ratings are released with the result and not before (BR-12, E8).

routesHere: retire this skill — it is no longer taught in class 8

request.text: skill wapas chalu kar do

steps.note: One step. It is retired rather than deleted, with a reason, and the ratings already given stay readable (BR-9).

plan.atomicity: One write: the retirement, its reason and the audit entry together or not at all. No new rating can be given against it. Every rating already given still reads, with the rubric that was in force when it was made (BR-9, BR-10) — a result from last term stays explainable.

errors.meaning: A skill was retired with no reason.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. A skill no longer taught and one wrongly defined mean different things to whoever reads the subject's skills next year.
Never describe retirement as deletion. There is no delete control (E7), and the ratings already given stay readable so an earlier result still explains itself (BR-9).
